bullets.title: Fed hikes 25bp; market expects another October hike—Goldman, JPM raise rate targets
bullets.body: The Fed raised rates 25bp this week (funds rate to 3.75-4.00%), triggering an initial selloff before markets stabilized. Goldman Sachs now expects an additional 25bp hike in October. JPM raised its YE26 2-year Treasury target +40bp to 4.70% and 10-year target +20bp to 5.05%; Morgan Stanley now models Fed hiking to 4.25-4.50% by March. Fed's Warsh messaging signals seriousness on price stability. 10-year yield is hovering near 4.96-4.98%, approaching cycle highs; Hedgeye sees signals pointing to 5.12%.

bullets.title: BOJ hikes 25bp to 1.25% (31-year high); yen paradoxically weakens on dovish dissents
bullets.body: The Bank of Japan raised its policy rate 25bp to 1.25% in a 7-2 vote, the highest level since 1995. Yen weakened ~1-1.25% against the USD following the decision as two dissenting votes were seen as dovish. Governor Ueda signaled data-dependent tightening ahead, did not exclude any policy options, warned against excessive tightening speed, and flagged Middle East/AI demand as monitoring factors. Citi forecasts additional BoJ hikes in December 2026 and March/July 2027.

bullets.title: ECB heading toward December hike; euro area inflation expectations hit survey highs
bullets.body: JPMorgan expects the ECB to hike again in December and March 2027, bringing the deposit rate to 3%. ECB Consumer Expectations Survey showed 5-year inflation expectations rose to 2.5%, the highest in the survey's history, despite unchanged near-term perceptions. ECB's Kaasik stressed avoiding second-round effects and signaled further restrictions if inflation risks materialize. Lagarde separately noted no signs of second-round effects 'so far.'

bullets.title: Synchronous Fed/ECB/BOJ tightening in the same month—first-ever occurrence—reshaping cross-asset views
bullets.body: The simultaneous rate hikes by Fed, ECB, and BOJ in September mark the first time all three major central banks tightened in the same month. Roth notes this is prompting a global reassessment of central bank policy paths with multiple further hikes expected from each. Germany's PPI surged to 4.6% YoY in August (vs. 3.9% estimate), and eurozone 1-year CPI expectations printed at 3.0%. UK August retail sales beat at +2.4% YoY vs. 1.9% estimate.

bullets.title: Geopolitical oil shock: Strait of Hormuz tanker traffic collapses, LNG becoming the harder problem
bullets.body: Commodity vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz dropped to 4 vessels Thursday vs. a 10-day average of 16. Saudi Arabia is routing larger volumes via Hormuz after East-West pipeline shutdown; Hormuz exports recovered to ~57% of pre-war volumes. Brent is near $104-106/bbl (~$16 risk premium over JPM $90 fair value per JPM) while WTI traded near $96-101 intraday. Jefferies notes LNG adaptation is proving harder than crude—European gas prices spiked from €30 to €80/MWh—while Houthi attacks diverted ~8% of global container capacity. UKMTO reported a tanker struck by unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz Friday morning.

bullets.title: S&P futures flat-to-up Friday; AI/semis leading recovery from early-week hawkish shock
bullets.body: S&P 500 futures traded +0.01-0.23% Friday morning after the S&P gained ~1.14% Thursday with Tech +2.2% and SOX +3.14%. The session is quad-witching with an S&P rebalance. Hedge funds added +1.4 standard deviations gross to US equities Thursday—concentrated in semis and memory—after de-risking ahead of the FOMC Wednesday. US L/S ratio now at 2.2, matching January-April AI bull market highs. JPM maintains a tactically cautious/neutral macro stance but is bullish on AI/Tech as a dip-buy.

bullets.title: Jensen Huang: NVDA chip shipments to double next year; AI compute demand set to far outpace supply
bullets.body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stated publicly that chip unit sales are expected to roughly double next year on broad AI adoption. Jefferies semis bus tour (13 companies) confirmed demand is set to far outpace supply across almost every semi product area over the next several quarters, with AI safety/alignment monitoring adding ~20% of incremental compute overhead. NVDA and AVGO emphasized model-release pacing is separate from inference monetization; hyperscaler bond issuance for AI infra is up 8x YoY despite 6-7.5% yields.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler AI capex commitments exceed $3T off-balance-sheet; Goldman forecasts $420B debt issuance in 2027
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs projects hyperscalers will issue ~$420B in gross IG debt in 2027, up 60% from ~$250B in 2026, reflecting upward CapEx revisions. AI-related debt issuance has already reached ~$578B YTD across hyperscalers, data center financing, infrastructure, and adjacent sectors. Hedgeye warns hyperscaler off-balance-sheet AI commitments exceed $3T, with $800B capex in 2026 and $1T+ projected for 2027, while OpenAI and Anthropic combined annualized revenue is only ~$105B.

bullets.title: GS equity team: S&P 500 'over-earning' but not in a bubble; AI capex tailwind fading 2028
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs estimates S&P 500 EPS grew 51% in 2Q26 and 26% over the past four quarters, forecasting 11% growth in 2027 ($415 EPS) and 2028 ($460 EPS). GS notes AI infrastructure spending accounted for nearly half of S&P 500 earnings growth in 2026 but expects this tailwind to fade—transitioning from an ~11pp earnings tailwind in 2026 to a marginal drag in 2028 as depreciation mounts. Hedgeye separately flags Shiller CAPE at 40.3 and US market cap/GDP at 240% vs. 150% at Dot Com peak, projecting high probability of Quad 4 drawdown in 1Q27.

bullets.title: Trump-Xi summit Sept 24 is 'low bar, high stakes'; tech/AI expected as focal point
bullets.body: JPMorgan describes the upcoming Trump-Xi summit on September 24 as 'low bar, high stakes' with tech and AI as focus points. Jefferies notes China is emerging as a key diplomatic actor in the Gulf crisis—Saudi Arabia reportedly appealed to Beijing to influence Tehran—and that the summit may offer a diplomatic 'clock' on the conflict. Iran has been granted US visas to attend the UN General Assembly next week, providing another diplomatic channel.

bullets.title: CoWoS demand-supply gap narrows to ~10%; leading-edge wafers and substrates now the bigger bottleneck
bullets.body: JPMorgan raised its CoWoS capacity estimates for TSMC by 4% in 2027 and 6% in 2028, bringing expected capacity to 200K/225K wfpm by end of 2027/28. The demand-supply gap has narrowed to ~10%, but leading-edge wafers and substrates are now cited as bigger bottlenecks than CoWoS capacity itself. AMD is reportedly planning a ~10% price hike on GPUs and AI chips in 4Q26 due to TSMC cost increases; silicon wafer price hikes of 20%+ are expected in 2027.

bullets.title: India buys record $15.2B in US Treasuries in July; China holdings hit lowest since GFC
bullets.body: India purchased a record $15.2B in US Treasuries in July, its largest monthly buy on record, signaling strong foreign central bank demand for dollar assets. Concurrently, China's US Treasury holdings have declined to the lowest level since the Global Financial Crisis.

bullets.title: EM equity funds snap 9-week inflow streak; Korea and Taiwan see heaviest outflows
bullets.body: EM equity funds posted $2.0B of outflows this week after nine consecutive weeks of inflows totaling $19.7B. Korea saw the heaviest sell-off at -$9.7B and Taiwan posted -$8.3B outflows, turning negative after six weeks of inflows. India remained negative for a third straight week (-$511M). Year-to-date EM equity fund flows remain solidly positive at +$72.5B.

bullets.title: Software earnings beat rate at 90%; infrastructure cohort leading applications 6.2% vs 4.2% T+7 returns
bullets.body: 90% of tracked software companies beat Q2 revenue expectations vs. an 83.7% historical average, with infrastructure software outperforming at 3.5% avg beat vs. 1.5% for applications. The median T+7 stock return was 5.4%, the strongest since inception of the tracker, with infrastructure up 6.2% vs. applications +4.2%. 50% of cohort posted true beat-and-raise, 300bps above the four-quarter average. SaaS-wide, the IGV ETF is down -3.9% YTD vs. S&P +12.7%.

bullets.title: Chase spending accelerated to +6.3% YoY MTD; all cohorts positive but gas prices at record highs weigh on DIY consumer
bullets.body: JPMorgan Chase card data shows spending accelerated to +6.3% YoY MTD through September 10 vs. +5.3% in August, with discretionary up 6.5% and non-discretionary up 5.6%. All income cohorts accelerated, with Gen Z/Millennials at +8.9% YoY. However, US national average gasoline prices hit $4.43/gallon (highest for this point in September ever), and diesel reached a record $6.40/gallon per AAA, pressuring lower-income DIY consumers and certain retail segments.

bullets.title: GLP-1 market: tirzepatide reaches 56.9% share; oral formulations reshaping demand with 34% of Wegovy scripts
bullets.body: Lilly tirzepatide market share increased to 56.9% (+0.3% over 4 weeks) vs. 49.5% a year ago; Novo semaglutide holds 37.0%. Overall GLP-1 TRx grew +5.4% YoY vs. -6.8% prior year as oral options broaden the market. Oral Wegovy scripts now represent 34% of total Wegovy scripts, and Foundayo accumulated 47K scripts since its April launch. Zepbound holds 60.7% of obesity market share.

bullets.title: AI agents pose systemic risk to telco/consumer ARPU; Meta Muse reaches #1 globally on App Store
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs and JPM tech strategists flag that Meta's Muse and similar AI agents can automate outbound calls to renegotiate bills, switch plans, and claim credits at scale—creating ARPU pressure for telcos, insurance, utilities, banks, and other subscription businesses. US telcos (AT&T -2%, Verizon -3%, T-Mobile -5.5%) traded down on this 'AI agent spindown' risk Thursday. Meta Muse separately reached #1 on the iOS App Store globally, surpassing ChatGPT.

bullets.title: Hedgeye risk ranges: SPX TREND turns Bullish; bond yields signaling higher cycle highs at 5.12% on 10Y
bullets.body: Hedgeye's Risk Range signals shifted SPX and NASDAQ Composite from Neutral to Bullish trend on September 18, alongside NVDA being upgraded to Bullish trend. VIX shifted from Bullish to Neutral as short-dated calendar vol dropped from 20 to 13 post-FOMC. However, Hedgeye maintains a bearish view on HYG/LQD credit and expects 2-year and 10-year yields to signal higher cycle highs at 4.85% and 5.12% respectively. SPX immediate-term risk range: 7,513-7,727.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley cuts US 2027 GDP to 2.3% on oil shock; core PCE to end 2026 at 3.2%
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley revised its US growth forecast down to 2.3% real GDP in 2027 (from 2.6%) and consumption growth to 1.8%, reflecting higher oil prices and two additional Fed hikes (December, March). Core PCE is now expected at 3.2% end-2026 and 2.7% end-2027. Non-residential fixed investment growth is lowered to 7.1% in 2027 as non-AI business investment recovery is delayed. Unemployment expected to rise to 4.3% with payrolls at ~50K/month in 2027.

bullets.title: Regional bank conference: consumer/commercial demand strong; NIM divergence emerging as deposit costs bite
bullets.body: All 11 regional bank presenters at this week's conference described consumer and commercial environments as strong (GDP ~2-2.5%, unemployment in low 4s), with C&I demand described as 'very strong.' However, NIM divergence is emerging: HBAN revised 2027 EPS guidance lower to $1.75-$1.83 from $1.90-$1.93 due to deposit cost pressure, while MTB, USB, and WAL remain confident in their NIM trajectories. KRE dropped 1.77% on Fed hawkishness, with larger regionals down 3-5%. Fed futures are pricing a 3rd hike in March and 4th in July 2027.
